tickets.title: The alarm's carried purchase records its order (**amendment 8, 2026-10-20**)

authority.locator: P67 · section 2 of amendment 8; P65 delivery review finding 1
authority.requirement: see amendment 8 section 2, ticket P67 (copied verbatim in the specification)

tickets.outcome: A purchase whose object reset at the wrong moment is credited once: the alarm that writes its outcome also remembers the order, so the same order re-sent later is dropped as a duplicate on both hosts.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a purchase of order X reset between the behaviour capture's admission and the outcome's, written by the alarm, leaves the order recorded as purchased: a later purchase of X under a new event id is dropped as duplicate_order and the ledger holds one outcome record for X (today: two).
criteria.proof: The P67 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P67.OM1 in src/units/P67 and they pass.

criteria.observable: Locks: the ordinary path's one-purchase-per-order rule (P40) unchanged; P65 RS1–RS3 and P64 unchanged; W06's digests and the idempotent replay unchanged (the record the alarm writes carries no stamp into any digest); no new remote call before any answer under the latency lever.
criteria.proof: The P67 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P67.OM2 in src/units/P67 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The released artifact shows the behaviour of every LOCAL criterion on both deployed shopper hosts.

existingEvidence.description: Reset during a purchase, alarm writes the outcome, re-send under a new id → two outcome records; controls: no reset → one; re-send before the alarm → one.

remainingWork: When the alarm admits a carried purchase outcome, record the order as the engine's own path does: the object host through its order memory (withOrder, src/reflex/core.ts), the session host through a write of the session record from the alarm via SessionManager (a new grant).

decisions.authorityRef: R-P155 under the owner's standing rule R-P78 (told, not asked)
decisions.effect: An advisory ticket: the fix records the order at the alarm on both hosts; the session host's write is granted here.

tickets.title: The kit's citations land and the override variables are typed (**amendment 8, 2026-10-20**)

authority.locator: P68 · section 2 of amendment 8; P63 and P62 delivery reviews
authority.requirement: see amendment 8 section 2, ticket P68 (copied verbatim in the specification)

tickets.outcome: An operator or a developer following the kit's citations lands on the construct named, and the learning-read override variables are part of the typed environment.

criteria.observable: Every citation in kit 02's render-acknowledgement paragraph (:933) and in the alarm-publication sentences (kit 02 :1171, kit 03 :1474-1488) names a line or range whose content is the construct the sentence describes at the artifact (a unit reads the kit and the source; RED today for the one citation still drifted at 8d07696f (ShopperReflex.ts:537 → :553; nine of the P63 report's fourteen were corrected by P65's kit commit, four never drifted on a construct reading)); kit 02 :1171 says what a skipped alarm still writes.
criteria.proof: The P68 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P68.KT1 in src/units/P68 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The override variables LIFT_WITNESS_BUDGET_MS and RING_READ_BUDGET_MS are declared in src/types/env.ts with their bounded-override semantics (a type-level unit); no served behaviour changes.
criteria.proof: The P68 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P68.KT2 in src/units/P68 and they pass.

criteria.observable: Locks: the kit-reading tests and every unit of amendments 5–7 unchanged; P62's override semantics unchanged; the kit line counts are STATED in the build and delivery reports, not locked by a unit (R-P162: P66 and P67 move kit 02 before P68 builds).
criteria.proof: The P68 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P68.KT3 in src/units/P68 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The released artifact shows the behaviour of every LOCAL criterion on both deployed shopper hosts.
